questions.question: How old was Fabian Hürzeler when Brighton appointed him manager in 2024?
questions.explanation: Thirty-one, a German who had just won promotion with St Pauli. He was younger than some of his own players.
questions.why: Brighton appointing a 31-year-old is the kind of bold move that makes fans of other clubs jealous.
questions.use: "Brighton hired a 31-year-old manager. Younger than some of the players."

questions.question: What is Chelsea's home ground called?
questions.explanation: Stamford Bridge. The ground opened in 1877 for athletics, and the football club came decades later, set up to fill it.
questions.why: A club invented to fill an empty stadium is the best Chelsea fact there is.
questions.use: "Stamford Bridge existed before Chelsea did. They started the club to fill it."

questions.question: In which year was Chelsea founded?
questions.explanation: 1905, in the Rising Sun pub opposite the ground, later renamed the Butcher's Hook. You can drink where the club was born.
questions.why: A club founded in a pub you can visit is a date-night fact.
questions.use: "Chelsea were founded in that pub opposite the ground. We should go for a drink there."

questions.question: What colour are Chelsea's home shirts?
questions.explanation: Royal blue, since around 1912. They began in a paler Eton blue, and until 1952 the team were nicknamed the Pensioners, after the old soldiers nearby.
questions.why: Knowing the team were once the Pensioners is the extra he won't expect.
questions.use: "Chelsea were nicknamed the Pensioners until the fifties. After the old soldiers down the road."

questions.question: Which Russian billionaire owned Chelsea from 2003 to 2022?
questions.explanation: Roman Abramovich, whose money turned a good club into a trophy machine: nineteen major trophies in nineteen years, and a lot of sacked managers. Forced to sell in 2022.
questions.why: Every Chelsea conversation splits into before and after Abramovich.
questions.use: Ask him: "Would Chelsea have won anything without Abramovich's money?"

questions.question: In which year did Chelsea first win the Champions League?
questions.explanation: 2012, in Munich, on penalties against Bayern in Bayern's own stadium, after a late equaliser. They had lost the 2008 final on penalties to United.
questions.why: Munich 2012 is the night Chelsea fans of a certain age will talk about for the rest of their lives.
questions.use: Ask him: "Munich 2012. Where were you for the penalties?"

questions.question: Who did Chelsea beat in the 2021 Champions League final?
questions.explanation: Manchester City, 1-0 in Porto, with a goal from Kai Havertz, under a manager who had been appointed that January.
questions.why: An all-English final is a thing fans compare notes on. Chelsea won this one.
questions.use: "Chelsea beat City in the 2021 final. Havertz, one-nil."

questions.question: In 2013, who overtook Bobby Tambling as Chelsea's top goalscorer?
questions.explanation: Frank Lampard, a midfielder, who finished on 211 goals before leaving in 2014. Strikers would take that number. He later managed the club, less successfully.
questions.why: A midfielder out-scoring the strikers is the Chelsea fact he will confirm proudly.
questions.use: "Lampard was a midfielder and scored 211 for Chelsea. Strikers would take that."

questions.question: Which manager won Chelsea back-to-back league titles in 2005 and 2006?
questions.explanation: José Mourinho, who arrived from Porto calling himself the Special One. First spell 2004 to 2007, second 2013 to 2015, another title in 2015.
questions.why: Mourinho is the manager Chelsea fans love and everyone else loves to hate. Know the name, know the era.
questions.use: Ask him: "Was Mourinho's first Chelsea team the best they've ever had?"

questions.question: In which year did Chelsea win their first league title?
questions.explanation: 1955, then a fifty-year wait for the second in 2005. Older fans lived through the whole gap.
questions.why: Fifty years between titles explains why the older fans are a bit giddy.
questions.use: "Chelsea won the league in 1955 and then not again until 2005. Fifty years."

questions.question: Which centre-back captained Chelsea for over a decade and was called Captain, Leader, Legend?
questions.explanation: John Terry, captain from 2004 to 2017, five league titles. The banner reads Captain, Leader, Legend. He also once wore a full kit to lift a trophy he hadn't played in.
questions.why: Terry divides opinion outside Chelsea and unites it inside. Both sides are worth hearing.
questions.use: Ask him: "Terry: greatest Chelsea captain or a bit much?"

questions.question: Which Ivorian striker scored in four FA Cup finals for Chelsea?
questions.explanation: Didier Drogba, who scored in final after final for Chelsea, a Champions League final among them. The definition of a big-game player.
questions.why: 'Big-game player' is a phrase he uses. Drogba is the picture in his head.
questions.use: "He's a bit of a Drogba, saves it for the big games."

questions.question: Which end of Chelsea's ground became home to the singing fans in the sixties?
questions.explanation: The Shed End. The old covered terrace was where the singing started in the sixties, and the name survived the rebuild in the 1990s.
questions.why: Stands with names are stands with reputations. The Shed is Chelsea's.
questions.use: "The Shed End. That's where the singing comes from."

questions.question: Which Italian manager won the league and cup double with Chelsea in 2010, scoring 103 league goals?
questions.explanation: Carlo Ancelotti, the calm one with the eyebrow. 103 goals was a Premier League season record at the time. Sacked the following year, in a corridor.
questions.why: Chelsea sacking title-winning managers is a running joke. Ancelotti is exhibit A.
questions.use: "Ancelotti won the double and got sacked a year later. In a corridor."

questions.question: Antonio Conte's title-winning Chelsea side of 2017 was famous for switching to which formation?
questions.explanation: 3-4-3, after a bad start. Three centre-backs, wing-backs flying forward. They won thirteen league games in a row and half the league copied it.
questions.why: If he says 'back three', this is where the modern fashion for it came from.
questions.use: "Conte's 3-4-3 in 2017 started the whole back-three fashion. Everyone copied it."

questions.question: Which manager led Chelsea Women to seven league titles before leaving in 2024?
questions.explanation: Emma Hayes, twelve years at the club, then off to coach the United States women's team, who won Olympic gold within months.
questions.why: Chelsea Women dominated for a decade. Knowing the manager's name is knowing the story.
questions.use: "Emma Hayes built Chelsea Women. Seven titles, then straight to Olympic gold with the USA."

questions.question: What is Chelsea's nickname?
questions.explanation: The Blues. The lion on the badge comes from the coat of arms of Earl Cadogan, the local landowner who was club president.
questions.why: Nickname and badge in one answer.
questions.use: "Come on you Blues." (The Chelsea version. Everton say the same, awkwardly.)

questions.question: Which Chelsea goalkeeper played on for years in a protective headguard after fracturing his skull?
questions.explanation: Petr Čech, injured in 2006, who kept playing for a decade in it. In the Munich final he saved a penalty in extra time and another in the shootout.
questions.why: The keeper in the helmet is a visual he will remember instantly.
questions.use: "Čech, the one with the headguard. Saved penalty after penalty in that Munich final."

questions.question: Which club's ground sits about two miles from Chelsea's?
questions.explanation: Fulham, a short trip along the river. Chelsea's own ground is actually in the borough of Fulham, which Fulham fans enjoy pointing out.
questions.why: West London derbies are gentle affairs, which he will deny.
questions.use: "The ground's technically in Fulham, not Chelsea. Don't tell him I said that."

questions.question: Which Italian became Chelsea's player-manager in 1998?
questions.explanation: Gianluca Vialli, who took over from Ruud Gullit and won two trophies within months while playing too. Chelsea of the late nineties were full of Italians.
questions.why: The Italian era, before the money, is what older fans mean when they say Chelsea were fun.
questions.use: Ask him: "Were the Zola and Vialli years the fun Chelsea, before the money?"

questions.question: Eden Hazard left Chelsea in 2019 to join which club?
questions.explanation: Real Madrid, after seven seasons and two league titles. He scored twice in his final Chelsea game, the Europa League final, then barely played in Spain.
questions.why: Hazard is the player Chelsea fans of the 2010s adored above all. His decline in Madrid is a sad coda.
questions.use: Ask him: "Was Hazard the best player you've watched at Chelsea?"

questions.question: What is Coventry City's nickname?
questions.explanation: The Sky Blues, a name the club took on in the early sixties, replacing the old one, the Bantams, along with new shirts and a song to match.
questions.why: Nickname, kit and song all trace to one man in the sixties. Handy.
questions.use: "Sky Blues. The kit, the nickname and the song all arrived together in the sixties."

questions.question: In which year did Coventry City win the FA Cup?
questions.explanation: 1987, won 3-2 after extra time at Wembley. The club's first major trophy, and by 2026 they had not won another. The city celebrated for a week.
questions.why: 1987 is the year every Coventry fan's story comes back to.
questions.use: Ask him: "Was anyone in your family at Wembley in 1987?"

questions.question: Who did Coventry beat in their FA Cup final win?
questions.explanation: Tottenham, who had won every FA Cup final they had reached until that day. The winner was a Spurs own goal off Gary Mabbutt's knee in extra time.
questions.why: The own goal off a knee is the detail fans savour. A Coventry fanzine was named after the knee.
questions.use: "Coventry won the cup with an own goal off a Spurs player's knee. There was a fanzine named after the knee."

questions.question: What colour was Coventry's famous away kit of 1978?
questions.explanation: Chocolate brown, worn away from home from 1978. It turns up on every bad-kit list going, and fans love it anyway.
questions.why: The brown kit is a cult object. Retro-shirt fans know it on sight.
questions.use: Ask him: "Would you actually wear the brown Coventry away kit?"

questions.question: Coventry City were founded in 1883 under what name?
questions.explanation: Singers FC, the works team of a bicycle factory. Coventry made bikes, then cars; the club followed the city.
questions.why: A club that began as a bicycle works team says everything about the city.
questions.use: "Coventry started as a bicycle factory's works team. Singers FC."

questions.question: Which manager and TV presenter changed Coventry's kit to sky blue and wrote the fans' song?
questions.explanation: Jimmy Hill, later the presenter of Match of the Day for decades, with the famous chin. He took Coventry from the third tier to the first in the 1960s.
questions.why: The man off the telly who built the club. Two facts for one.
questions.use: Ask him: "Did you know Jimmy Hill off Match of the Day basically invented modern Coventry?"

questions.question: What was Coventry's home ground from 1899 to 2005?
questions.explanation: Highfield Road, close to the city centre, for 106 years. It is housing now.
questions.why: Old grounds are where fans keep their childhood. Naming this one earns a story.
questions.use: Ask him: "Did you ever go to Highfield Road?"

questions.question: In 1981 Highfield Road became the first English ground to be what?
questions.explanation: All-seater, at the chairman's insistence. The fans hated sitting down and the terraces came back within a few years.
questions.why: Being first at something everyone now does, and having it rejected, is a great trivia shape.
questions.use: "Coventry were the first all-seater ground in England, in 1981. Fans hated it so much they put terraces back."

questions.question: When Coventry went down in 2001, how many consecutive seasons had they spent in the top flight?
questions.explanation: Thirty-four seasons, from 1967 to 2001, escaping relegation on the final day more than once. Just Arsenal, Everton and Liverpool had a longer unbroken run at the time.
questions.why: Thirty-four years of survival is the club's proudest habit, and then the fall.
questions.use: "Coventry spent thirty-four years in the top flight and kept surviving on the final day. Then they went down and kept going."

questions.question: Coventry's stadium opened in 2005 under which sponsor's name?
questions.explanation: Ricoh, the Japanese office-equipment firm. It became the Coventry Building Society Arena in 2021. The club has twice been locked out of it in rent disputes.
questions.why: A club locked out of its own stadium twice is a story people struggle to believe.
questions.use: "They've been locked out of their own stadium twice. Rent rows."

questions.question: In 2013-14 Coventry played home games in which town because of a rent dispute?
questions.explanation: Northampton, 35 miles away. Fans boycotted, crowds fell to two thousand, and people protested outside the empty stadium back home.
questions.why: The exile years are the wound. Knowing about them is knowing what the club survived.
questions.use: Ask him: "Did you boycott the Northampton games or go anyway?"

questions.question: From 2019 to 2021 Coventry shared a ground with which club?
questions.explanation: Birmingham City, at St Andrew's, twenty miles away. They won promotion to the Championship while homeless, and many fans could not get there.
questions.why: Promotion while exiled is the kind of achievement only the fans who lived it can weigh.
questions.use: "Coventry won promotion while playing home games at Birmingham. Fans couldn't even get in."

questions.question: Which manager took Coventry from League Two to a Championship play-off final?
questions.explanation: Mark Robins, back for a second spell from 2017 to 2024. Two promotions, one of them won in exile, and a Wembley final.
questions.why: Robins is the name every Coventry fan says with gratitude.
questions.use: "Mark Robins took them from the fourth tier to a play-off final. Some of it without a home ground."

questions.question: Coventry lost the 2023 Championship play-off final on penalties to which club?
questions.explanation: Luton Town, after a 1-1 draw at Wembley and a shootout that went to sudden death. One penalty from the Premier League.
questions.why: The near miss makes the eventual promotion sweeter. He will want to tell you both halves.
questions.use: Ask him: "Was the Luton final the worst day you've had as a fan?"

questions.question: In which year were Coventry promoted back to the Premier League as Championship champions?
questions.explanation: 2026, with 95 points, their first top-flight season since 2001. Twenty-five years, a spell in the fourth tier and two exiles in between.
questions.why: This is the freshest joy in the fanbase. Ask about it and make his day.
questions.use: Ask him: "Where were you when they went up as champions?"

questions.question: Coventry is in which region of England?
questions.explanation: The West Midlands, twenty miles from Birmingham. A car-making city with a cathedral rebuilt after the war.
questions.why: Map first, football second.
questions.use: "Coventry, West Midlands. Twenty minutes from Birmingham."

questions.question: What is Coventry's derby with Leicester City called?
questions.explanation: The M69 derby, after the motorway linking the two cities, about 25 miles apart. Aston Villa and Birmingham are the other Midlands grudges.
questions.why: Rivalries named after roads are a very English thing. Knowing this one shows you've done your homework.
questions.use: Ask him: "The M69 derby. Is Leicester the one that really matters, or Villa?"

questions.question: Which striker shared the Premier League Golden Boot in 1998 with eighteen goals for Coventry?
questions.explanation: Dion Dublin, level with Michael Owen and Chris Sutton. He later became a TV presenter and invented a percussion instrument called the Dube.
questions.why: A Golden Boot winner who invented a drum is the fact that wins the table.
questions.use: "Dion Dublin won the Golden Boot at Coventry and then invented a drum. Called the Dube."

questions.question: Which former England midfielder took over as Coventry manager in November 2024?
questions.explanation: Frank Lampard, whose managing career had stalled at Chelsea and Everton. Coventry were two points above the relegation zone when he arrived.
questions.why: Lampard at Coventry is a redemption story fans of every club followed.
questions.use: Ask him: "Did Coventry finally prove Lampard can manage?"

questions.question: The Sky Blue Song is sung to the tune of what?
questions.explanation: The Eton Boating Song, a rowing song from the posh school. The club's manager co-wrote the football words in 1962 and fans have sung it ever since.
questions.why: Working-class fans singing an Eton rowing song is a lovely contradiction to have in your pocket.
questions.use: "The Coventry song is the Eton Boating Song with new words, from 1962."

questions.question: What is Crystal Palace's home ground called?
questions.explanation: Selhurst Park, home since 1924. Old, cramped and loud, with one end full of drums and flags.
questions.why: Selhurst's atmosphere is the thing rival fans concede. Mention it and he lights up.
questions.use: "Selhurst on a night game. Best atmosphere in London, they say."

questions.question: What is Crystal Palace's nickname?
questions.explanation: The Eagles, since 1973. Before that they were the Glaziers, after the glass palace the club is named for.
questions.why: Two nicknames, one club. The old one explains the name.
questions.use: "They were the Glaziers before the Eagles. Because of the glass palace."

questions.question: Who are Crystal Palace's arch-rivals?
questions.explanation: Brighton, forty miles down the M23. It began with two managers feuding in the 1970s and the fans took it on. Nobody outside quite understands it.
questions.why: The rivalry that makes no geographical sense is the one worth knowing about.
questions.use: Ask him: "Why Brighton? They're forty miles away."

questions.question: What colours are Palace's home shirts?
questions.explanation: Red and blue vertical stripes, copied from Barcelona in the 1970s by a manager who admired them.
questions.why: Barcelona's colours in south London is a fact that surprises people.
questions.use: "Palace's stripes are copied from Barcelona. A manager just liked them in the seventies."

questions.question: In which year was the professional Crystal Palace club formed?
questions.explanation: 1905, by the company that owned the Crystal Palace. In 2022 the club put 1861 on its badge, after an amateur side of that name, which historians dispute.
questions.why: The club is named after a building, and the building came first.
questions.use: "Palace were formed in 1905, but the club counts from 1861. Ask a historian and it gets heated."

questions.question: Which final did the Crystal Palace grounds host every year from 1895 to 1914?
questions.explanation: The FA Cup final, with some crowds topping 100,000. The glass palace burned down in 1936, but the club kept the name and the building is drawn on the badge.
questions.why: A club named after a building that no longer exists is a story people enjoy.
questions.use: "The FA Cup final used to be played at the Crystal Palace. That's where the club came from."

questions.question: Which former England manager, a Palace fan as a boy, took charge of the club in 2017?
questions.explanation: Roy Hodgson, who grew up in Croydon and watched Palace from the terraces. He kept them up four years running and came back for a second spell at 75.
questions.why: A boyhood fan managing the club at 70 is a warm story fans love telling.
questions.use: Ask him: "Hodgson managing his boyhood club in his seventies, was that lovely or a bit much?"

questions.question: Palace lost FA Cup finals in 1990 and 2016 to the same club. Which?
questions.explanation: Manchester United both times: after a replay in 1990, in extra time in 2016. Palace led in both.
questions.why: Two finals lost to the same club in the same way is the kind of pain that bonds fans.
questions.use: "United beat them in two cup finals, 1990 and 2016. Palace led in both."

questions.question: Palace won the 2025 FA Cup, then UEFA moved them out of the Europa League. Why?
questions.explanation: A co-owner also held a stake in Lyon, who had qualified too, and UEFA's rules bar clubs with shared owners. Palace went down to the Conference League.
questions.why: Winning your first trophy and then being demoted in Europe over ownership is the sore point.
questions.use: Ask him: "Was the UEFA ownership ruling as unfair as Palace fans say?"

questions.question: Who scored the winning goal in the 2025 FA Cup final?
questions.explanation: Eberechi Eze, a local boy, in the first half. Goalkeeper Dean Henderson then saved a penalty and should probably have been sent off earlier.
questions.why: The scorer of the first trophy-winning goal is a name fans will hold onto for life.
questions.use: "Eze scored the goal that won Palace their first trophy. Local lad too."

questions.question: Wilfried Zaha, who played over 450 games for Palace, left in 2023 for which club?
questions.explanation: Galatasaray in Turkey, after two spells and a decade as the club's talisman. An unhappy year at Manchester United sits in between.
questions.why: Zaha is the modern Palace hero. If he mentions one player from the 2010s, it is him.
questions.use: Ask him: "Was Zaha the best player Palace have ever had?"

questions.question: Which striker scored twice off the bench in the 1990 FA Cup final for Palace?
questions.explanation: Ian Wright, playing on a leg broken weeks earlier. The final was drawn 3-3 and Palace lost the replay. Wright later became an Arsenal legend and a TV presenter.
questions.why: Ian Wright off the telly was a Palace hero first. That surprises people.
questions.use: "Ian Wright started at Palace. Scored twice in a cup final on a half-healed broken leg."

questions.question: What was the name of the real eagle that flew around Selhurst Park before matches?
questions.explanation: Kayla, an American bald eagle, who did a lap of the ground before kick-off from 2010 until she died in 2020.
questions.why: A live eagle at a football match is the fact nobody believes until you show them.
questions.use: "Palace had an actual eagle flying round the pitch before games. Called Kayla."

questions.question: Crystal Palace are from which part of London?
questions.explanation: South London, around Croydon and Selhurst. The other big south London clubs, Millwall and Charlton, are rivals too.
questions.why: London's football map is confusing. South is Palace territory.
questions.use: "Palace are south London. Croydon, basically."

questions.question: Who scored the extra-time winner in Palace's 4-3 FA Cup semi-final against Liverpool in 1990?
questions.explanation: Alan Pardew, a midfielder who later came back to manage the club and took them to the 2016 final. Liverpool had beaten Palace 9-0 earlier that season.
questions.why: Beating Liverpool 4-3 months after losing 9-0 to them is a story fans tell in full.
questions.use: Ask him: "Do Palace fans bring up the 4-3 against Liverpool in 1990?"

questions.question: Which former Arsenal captain managed Palace from 2021 to 2023?
questions.explanation: Patrick Vieira, who made Palace young and stylish for a season, then got sacked after twelve games without a win.
questions.why: Vieira's Palace was briefly the neutral's favourite. The ending was less romantic.
questions.use: "Vieira made Palace watchable for a year. Then twelve games without a win."

questions.question: The fan group behind the drums and flags at Selhurst Park is called what?
questions.explanation: The Holmesdale Fanatics, named after the stand they fill. They organise the displays, the drums and the songs, European-style.
questions.why: If he mentions 'the Fanatics', this is who he means.
questions.use: "That's the Holmesdale Fanatics with the drums. They run the atmosphere."

questions.question: Palace won promotion to the Premier League in 2004 by beating which club in the play-off final?
questions.explanation: West Ham, 1-0 in Cardiff, with a goal from Neil Shipperley. Palace had been near the bottom of the division at Christmas.
questions.why: Bottom at Christmas to promoted in May: the comeback fans measure others against.
questions.use: "Palace were nearly bottom of the second tier at Christmas 2003 and went up that May."

questions.question: Which Austrian manager won the FA Cup with Palace in 2025?
questions.explanation: Oliver Glasner, who had already won the Europa League with Eintracht Frankfurt. He took Palace to their first trophy in his first full season.
questions.why: Glasner is the name on the first trophy. He will always be a Palace legend for it.
questions.use: "Glasner won them the cup in 2025. Their first major trophy."

questions.question: Palace beat which club in the 2025 FA Cup final?
questions.explanation: Manchester City, 1-0, at Wembley. City had won the cup two years earlier and were favourites by a distance.
questions.why: Beating City in a final is the giant-killing every small club dreams of. Palace did it.
questions.use: "They beat City in the final. Actual Man City, one-nil."

questions.question: Which ground was Everton's home from 1892 to 2025?
questions.explanation: Goodison Park, one of the first purpose-built football grounds in England. Everton left it in 2025 after 133 years.
questions.why: Leaving Goodison was emotional for every Everton fan. Knowing it shows you understand.
questions.use: Ask him: "Did you go to Goodison before they left? What was it like?"

questions.question: What is Everton's nickname?
questions.explanation: The Toffees, after the toffee shops by the club's early grounds. The Toffee Lady, in old-fashioned dress, throws sweets into the crowd before home games.
questions.why: The Toffee Lady is the detail that makes rival fans smile too.
questions.use: "The Toffee Lady throws sweets into the crowd before games. That's why they're the Toffees."

questions.question: Who are Everton's rivals in the Merseyside derby?
questions.explanation: Liverpool, whose ground sat across Stanley Park from Everton's old one. The friendly derby, as families are split, though it's famous for red cards.
questions.why: A friendly derby famous for red cards is the contradiction worth quoting.
questions.use: "They call it the friendly derby, and it's famous for red cards."

questions.question: In which year was Everton founded?
questions.explanation: 1878, as St Domingo's, a church team. They renamed themselves Everton a year later and were founder members of the Football League in 1888.
questions.why: Everton were there at the start of league football. Fans are proud of the age.
questions.use: "Everton go back to 1878. Founder members of the league."

questions.question: What colour are Everton's home shirts?
questions.explanation: Royal blue, since 1901. Before that they tried black with a red sash, and were nicknamed the Black Watch.
questions.why: Blue in Liverpool means Everton. Red means the other lot.
questions.use: "Blue half of Liverpool. Everton."

questions.question: Which centre-forward scored 383 goals for Everton between the wars?
questions.explanation: Dixie Dean, famous for his heading, in the 1920s and 30s. A statue of him went up outside the old ground in 2001. He died there, watching a derby, in 1980.
questions.why: Dixie Dean is the name older Evertonians say like a saint's.
questions.use: "Dixie Dean died at the ground, watching a derby. That's devotion."

questions.question: In 1927-28 Everton's centre-forward scored how many league goals?
questions.explanation: Sixty, in 39 games. He got the sixtieth, a header, in the final match of the season, against Arsenal.
questions.why: Sixty in a season is a number that ends arguments about modern strikers.
questions.use: "Sixty league goals in one season, 1928. Imagine a striker doing that now."

questions.question: In which year did Everton win the league title, the ninth in the club's history?
questions.explanation: 1987, two years after the eighth. By 2025, four clubs had won more league titles than Everton's nine.
questions.why: Nine titles is the number that makes Everton a big club, whatever recent years suggest.
questions.use: "Nine league titles. People forget how big Everton were."

questions.question: Who managed Everton through their 1980s glory years?
questions.explanation: Howard Kendall: two league titles, an FA Cup and a European trophy in the mid-eighties. Then the European ban after Heysel stopped the team going any further.
questions.why: The mid-eighties team is the one older fans mean when they say Everton were the best in England.
questions.use: Ask him: "How good would Kendall's Everton have been without the European ban?"

questions.question: Which European trophy did Everton win in 1985?
questions.explanation: The Cup Winners' Cup, beating Rapid Vienna 3-1 in Rotterdam. Weeks later English clubs were banned from Europe for five years.
questions.why: Everton's European trophy came just before the door shut. It shapes how fans see what might have been.
questions.use: "Everton won in Europe in 1985 and then English clubs got banned for five years. Terrible timing."

questions.question: In which year did Everton win the FA Cup, the club's fifth?
questions.explanation: 1995, beating Manchester United 1-0 at Wembley with a Paul Rideout header. No major trophy followed in the thirty years to 2025.
questions.why: The trophy drought is the sore point. Handle with care and sympathy.
questions.use: "The 1995 cup, and then a very long wait. Not that anyone's counting."

questions.question: Which 16-year-old's first Everton goal, in 2002, ended Arsenal's thirty-game unbeaten run?
questions.explanation: Wayne Rooney, five days before his seventeenth birthday. He left for Manchester United two years later, which Evertonians did not enjoy.
questions.why: Rooney is Everton's best-known product and its sorest departure.
questions.use: Ask him: "Do Everton fans forgive Rooney for leaving, or not?"

questions.question: Which Scottish manager called Everton 'the People's Club' on his first day in 2002?
questions.explanation: David Moyes, who made Everton hard to beat for eleven years before leaving for Manchester United in 2013.
questions.why: 'The People's Club' is a phrase Evertonians adopted. Use it and he'll know you did your homework.
questions.use: "The People's Club. Moyes said it on his first day in 2002."

questions.question: By 2025, how many times had Everton been relegated from the top flight?
questions.explanation: Twice, in 1930 and 1951, and they came back up each time. By 2025 they had spent over 120 seasons in the top flight.
questions.why: It is the stat Everton fans reach for when the club is struggling.
questions.use: "By 2025 Everton had been relegated twice in their whole history. Twice."

questions.question: The tower on Everton's badge was built as what?
questions.explanation: A village lock-up, Prince Rupert's Tower, built in 1787 to hold drunks overnight. It stands in the Everton district and has been on the badge since 1938.
questions.why: A jail for drunks on the badge is the fact that gets a laugh at any table.
questions.use: "The tower on the Everton badge is an old lock-up for drunks. True story."

questions.question: Everton's new stadium, opened in 2025, is built where?
questions.explanation: Bramley-Moore Dock, on the Mersey waterfront north of the city centre. A filled-in dock, with the river behind one stand.
questions.why: The new ground is the big Everton topic of the decade. Knowing where it is shows you've kept up.
questions.use: Ask him: "Have you been to the new ground yet? Is it as good as they say?"

questions.question: Which ground was Everton's home from 1884 to 1892?
questions.explanation: Anfield. Everton walked out over rent, and the landlord started a new club to play there: Liverpool. Earlier homes were Stanley Park and Priory Road.
questions.why: Liverpool only exist because Everton fell out with a landlord. Evertonians love this.
questions.use: "Everton were at Anfield first. They left over rent and the landlord started Liverpool."

questions.question: Tim Cahill, who punched the corner flag when he scored, came from which country?
questions.explanation: Australia. Fifty-six Premier League goals for Everton, a lot of them headers, each celebrated by boxing the corner flag.
questions.why: The corner-flag celebration is a visual he can picture instantly.
questions.use: "Cahill. The one who used to box the corner flag."

questions.question: In which position did Everton finish in 2005, earning a Champions League qualifying place?
questions.explanation: Fourth, above Liverpool, who then went and won the Champions League that very season. Everton lost their qualifier and went out. Evertonians do not enjoy this story.
questions.why: The 2005 story is the purest example of Everton luck. Tell it gently.
questions.use: "Everton finished above Liverpool in 2005 and Liverpool won the Champions League anyway. Typical."

questions.question: At Everton's old ground, which end did the home side like to attack in the second half?
questions.explanation: The Gwladys Street End, where the home fans stood. Kicking towards it late on meant the noise could push the team on.
questions.why: Stands with names carry memories. This one is now history.
questions.use: Ask him: "Did you ever stand in the Gwladys Street? What was it like at the end?"

questions.question: What is Fulham's home ground called?
questions.explanation: Craven Cottage, on the bank of the Thames, with a real cottage in one corner where the players' families sit.
questions.why: The prettiest ground in London, and the cottage is real. Easy win.
questions.use: "Craven Cottage. There's an actual cottage in the corner. Families sit on the balcony."

questions.question: What is Fulham's nickname?
questions.explanation: The Cottagers, from the ground's name. Also, more plainly, the Whites.
questions.why: Nickname and ground are the same story here.
questions.use: "The Cottagers. It really is just because of the ground."

questions.question: In which year was Fulham founded?
questions.explanation: 1879, as a church Sunday school team, which makes Fulham older than Spurs (1882), Arsenal (1886) and Chelsea (1905).
questions.why: Being older than the London giants is something Fulham fans enjoy quietly.
questions.use: "Fulham are older than Arsenal, Spurs and Chelsea. 1879."

questions.question: What colours are Fulham's home kit?
questions.explanation: White shirts, black shorts. Plain and old-fashioned, like the ground.
questions.why: Kit recognition, the everyday skill.
questions.use: "White with black shorts. That's Fulham, not Spurs."

questions.question: Which Egyptian businessman owned Fulham from 1997 to 2013?
questions.explanation: Mohamed Al-Fayed, who also owned Harrods. He took Fulham from the third tier to the Premier League and a European final.
questions.why: The Harrods owner is the Fulham fact everyone half-remembers.
questions.use: Ask him: "Was Fulham under Al-Fayed as mad as it sounds?"

questions.question: A statue of which pop star stood outside Fulham's ground from 2011 to 2013?
questions.explanation: Michael Jackson, a friend of the owner who had watched one match there. Fans were baffled; the next owner removed it and it spent five years in a football museum.
questions.why: It is one of the strangest things ever to happen at a football ground. Enjoy it.
questions.use: "Fulham had a Michael Jackson statue outside the ground for two years. He'd been to one game."

questions.question: In which year did Fulham reach the Europa League final?
questions.explanation: 2010, losing 2-1 to Atlético Madrid in Hamburg in extra time. On the way they beat Juventus from 4-1 down on aggregate. A tiny club's greatest run.
questions.why: The 2010 run is the story Fulham fans tell above all others.
questions.use: Ask him: "The 2010 Europa League run. Where were you for the Juventus game?"

questions.question: Who managed Fulham to their Europa League final?
questions.explanation: Roy Hodgson, calm and clever, who was named manager of the year for it and then took the Liverpool job, which went badly.
questions.why: Hodgson at Fulham is the high point of a long career. Fans remember him fondly.
questions.use: "Hodgson got Fulham to a European final. Then Liverpool happened."

questions.question: Which American businessman bought Fulham in 2013?
questions.explanation: Shahid Khan, who had bought the NFL's Jacksonville Jaguars the year before and has a famous moustache.
questions.why: The moustache and the NFL team: two facts he will confirm.
questions.use: "Khan bought Fulham in 2013. The American with the moustache and the NFL team."

questions.question: Fans walking to Fulham's ground from the Tube usually go through which park?
questions.explanation: Bishop's Park, the riverside park beside the ground. Home and away fans stroll through it together from Putney Bridge station.
questions.why: A ground reached through a park by the river is a day out. Suggest it.
questions.use: "We could walk through Bishop's Park and along the river before the game."

questions.question: Fulham won the second tier as champions in 2001 under which French manager?
questions.explanation: Jean Tigana, with 101 points, playing passing football. It took Fulham back to the top flight for the first time since 1968.
questions.why: Tigana's team was the start of modern Fulham. The older fans light up at his name.
questions.use: Ask him: "Was Tigana's Fulham the best team the club's had?"

questions.question: Which Portuguese manager won the Championship with Fulham in 2022?
questions.explanation: Marco Silva, with 90 points and a striker scoring goals for fun. Fulham had bounced between divisions for years; Silva made them stay.
questions.why: Silva ended the yo-yo years. That is why fans speak well of him.
questions.use: "Silva stopped them yo-yoing. They stayed up comfortably after that."

questions.question: Who are Fulham's main London rivals?
questions.explanation: Chelsea, under two miles away. Chelsea's ground is actually in Fulham, which Fulham fans mention. Brentford and QPR are the other local grudges.
questions.why: West London's rivalries are gentle by the standards of the game, and he will insist otherwise.
questions.use: "Stamford Bridge is in Fulham, you know. Don't tell a Chelsea fan."

questions.question: Which Fulham legend became the first footballer paid £100 a week, in 1961?
questions.explanation: Johnny Haynes, an England captain who played 658 games for Fulham from 1952 to 1970. A stand is named after him and his statue is outside.
questions.why: The first hundred-pound-a-week footballer is a fact that reaches beyond football.
questions.use: "The first footballer to earn a hundred pounds a week played for Fulham. Johnny Haynes, 1961."

questions.question: Which American's chipped goal finished Fulham's comeback against Juventus in the Europa League?
questions.explanation: Clint Dempsey, with a chipped finish to complete a comeback from 4-1 down on aggregate. Fulham's greatest night by common agreement.
questions.why: The Dempsey chip is the goal Fulham fans replay in their heads.
questions.use: "Dempsey's chip against Juventus. That's the one they all talk about."

questions.question: Fulham first played at their riverside ground in which decade?
questions.explanation: The 1890s. Fulham moved in in 1896, when the site was overgrown. Apart from two seasons sharing QPR's ground in the 2000s, it has been home since.
questions.why: A ground used since Victorian times is a big part of why fans love it.
questions.use: Ask him: "Didn't Fulham have to play at QPR for a couple of years?"

questions.question: Fulham's rebuilt Riverside Stand, opened in 2024, was designed to include what unusual feature?
questions.explanation: A rooftop swimming pool, alongside restaurants and a members' club, at prices that made ordinary fans wince.
questions.why: A pool at a football ground is a fact that stops a table.
questions.use: "Fulham's new stand has a rooftop pool. At a football stadium."

questions.question: Which Fulham striker scored 43 goals in the 2021-22 Championship season?
questions.explanation: Aleksandar Mitrović, a Serbian striker who scored like a machine in the second tier and celebrated every one like a final. He left for Saudi Arabia in 2023.
questions.why: Mitrović is the modern Fulham hero. His 43 is a number fans quote.
questions.use: "Mitrović got 43 in one Championship season. Forty-three."

questions.question: Fulham are from which part of London?
questions.explanation: South-west London, in the borough of Hammersmith and Fulham, on a bend of the Thames.
questions.why: Placing the club on the map is the basic courtesy.
questions.use: "South-west London, by the river. Nice part of town."

questions.question: What is Fulham's mascot called?
questions.explanation: Billy the Badger, who was once ordered off the pitch by a referee for breakdancing in the corner during a match.
questions.why: A mascot sent off for breakdancing is the ideal dull-match anecdote.
questions.use: "Fulham's mascot got sent off once. For breakdancing during the game."

questions.question: What is Hull City's nickname?
questions.explanation: The Tigers, a name from the club's first years. Commentators use it as often as the club's real name.
questions.why: Hear 'the Tigers' on the telly and you'll know it's his lot.
questions.use: "The Tigers. Easy one to remember."

questions.question: What is Hull City's home ground called?
questions.explanation: The MKM Stadium, since 2002, shared with the rugby league club Hull FC. It opened as the KC Stadium; sponsors change, the building doesn't.
questions.why: Ground names change with sponsors. Knowing that stops you sounding out of date either way.
questions.use: "The MKM. Used to be the KC. Same place."

questions.question: What colours are Hull's home shirts?
questions.explanation: Amber and black stripes, worn since the club's earliest days.
questions.why: Kit recognition on a small screen is the skill that lets you follow along.
questions.use: "Amber and black. That's Hull."

questions.question: In which year was Hull City founded?
questions.explanation: 1904. Hull was a rugby league city and the football club took decades to catch on. It took them 104 years to reach the top division.
questions.why: A football club in a rugby town explains a lot about Hull's history.
questions.use: "Hull's a rugby city. The football club took a hundred and four years to reach the top flight."

questions.question: Which club did Hull beat at Wembley in the 2008 play-off final?
questions.explanation: Bristol City, 1-0, in front of about 86,000. It took Hull into the top division for the first time in their history.
questions.why: 2008 is Hull's year zero. Every fan over thirty has a story about it.
questions.use: Ask him: "Where were you for the 2008 play-off final?"

questions.question: Who scored the winning goal in Hull's 2008 play-off final?
questions.explanation: Dean Windass, a 39-year-old born in Hull who had been released by the club as a teenager, with a volley from the edge of the box. He wept on the pitch.
questions.why: A local boy, 39, released as a kid, scoring the goal that took his hometown up. The perfect football story.
questions.use: "The winner in 2008 was scored by a 39-year-old from Hull who the club had released as a teenager."

questions.question: Which manager took Hull into the Premier League in 2008?
questions.explanation: Phil Brown, remembered for his suntan, his headset and one very public team talk. He sang to the fans on the pitch when they stayed up.
questions.why: Brown is a character. Fans of other clubs mock him; Hull fans mostly love him.
questions.use: "Phil Brown. The one with the tan and the headset."

questions.question: In 2008 Hull's manager gave a half-time team talk on the pitch. At which club's ground?
questions.explanation: Manchester City's, on Boxing Day, 4-0 down at the break. He sat the players on the grass and lectured them. It finished 5-1; later he said he'd change nothing.
questions.why: The on-pitch team talk is one of the strangest sights in Premier League history. Worth knowing the details.
questions.use: "Hull's manager once did the half-time team talk on the pitch, in front of the fans. Sat them all down. They lost 5-1."

questions.question: Hull reached the FA Cup final in 2014 and lost to which club?
questions.explanation: Arsenal, 3-2 after extra time, and Hull had led 2-0 inside eight minutes. It was the club's first FA Cup final.
questions.why: Two-nil up in a cup final and losing is the kind of pain fans carry for life.
questions.use: Ask him: "2014, two-nil up at Wembley after eight minutes. Do you ever think about it?"

questions.question: Who managed Hull in the 2014 FA Cup final?
questions.explanation: Steve Bruce, the former Manchester United captain. Because the winners were already in the Champions League, losing the final put Hull into Europe for the first time.
questions.why: Losing a final and qualifying for Europe anyway is a quirk fans enjoy explaining.
questions.use: "Hull got into Europe by losing a cup final. The winners were already qualified."

questions.question: In 2013 Hull's owners tried to rename the club. The FA refused. What did they want to drop?
questions.explanation: 'City'. The owners called the word common. Fans marched, the FA said no, and the row with the owners ran on for years.
questions.why: Fans fighting their own owners over the club's name is a story every supporter understands.
questions.use: Ask him: "Were you part of the protests when the owners tried to take 'City' out of the name?"

questions.question: What was Hull's home ground before 2002?
questions.explanation: Boothferry Park, from 1946, which had its own railway station and, by the end, a supermarket built into one stand.
questions.why: A ground with a supermarket in it is a fact people remember.
questions.use: "Hull's old ground had a supermarket built into one of the stands. Boothferry Park."

questions.question: Hull is in which historic county?
questions.explanation: Yorkshire, the East Riding. The city's full name is Kingston upon Hull, and it sits where the River Hull meets the Humber.
questions.why: Yorkshire loyalty runs deep. Getting the county right matters.
questions.use: "Hull's Yorkshire. East Riding, on the Humber."

questions.question: Which club do Hull fans regard as their main rivals?
questions.explanation: Leeds United, the big club sixty miles west. Grimsby, over the Humber, is the older, smaller grudge.
questions.why: Rivalries tell you who he shouts at. Leeds is the answer here.
questions.use: "Hull and Leeds. Two cities, one long grudge."

questions.question: Which Portuguese manager led Hull in the Premier League in 2016-17?
questions.explanation: Marco Silva, in his first English job. Hull went down anyway, but his reputation survived and he went on to manage Watford, Everton and Fulham.
questions.why: Silva is a name he will know from bigger clubs. Hull is where England first saw him.
questions.use: "Marco Silva started in England at Hull. Didn't keep them up, but everyone noticed him."

questions.question: After relegation from the Premier League in 2017, Hull dropped to League One in which year?
questions.explanation: 2020, finishing bottom of the Championship in the pandemic season. Two relegations in three years.
questions.why: The fall to the third tier is the low point fans measure the current club against.
questions.use: Ask him: "How bad was the League One year? Did you keep going?"

questions.question: Who managed Hull to the League One title?
questions.explanation: Grant McCann, a Northern Irish former midfielder, who took them up as champions at the first attempt.
questions.why: Bouncing straight back is the happy half of the story. Fans like being reminded.
questions.use: "Grant McCann took them straight back up as champions. Didn't hang about."

questions.question: Which Turkish television personality bought Hull City in 2022?
questions.explanation: Acun Ilıcalı, the face of Turkey's version of Survivor, who built his own TV network. He promised the Premier League and, in the end, delivered it.
questions.why: A Turkish TV star buying an English club is a fact that stops a conversation.
questions.use: "Hull were bought by the man behind Survivor in Turkey. Basically Turkish Ant and Dec."

questions.question: In which year did Hull return to the Premier League for the first time since 2017?
questions.explanation: 2026, through the play-offs after finishing sixth in the Championship. Nine years away, including one in the third tier.
questions.why: The 2026 promotion is the one fans will talk about for years. Ask about it.
questions.use: Ask him: "Where were you when they went up through the play-offs this time?"

questions.question: What is Hull City's mascot called?
questions.explanation: Roary, a tiger in the club kit, who works the touchline before kick-off and at half-time.
questions.why: Mascots are safe ground when the match goes quiet.
questions.use: "Roary. Of course the tiger's called Roary."

questions.question: What is Ipswich Town's home ground called?
questions.explanation: Portman Road, the club's home since 1884, a short walk from the town centre and the railway station.
questions.why: A ground in the middle of town makes match day easy. Handy if he ever takes you.
questions.use: "Portman Road. They've played there since 1884."

questions.question: What is Ipswich Town's nickname?
questions.explanation: The Tractor Boys. Rival fans meant it as a jibe about the farming county around the town; Ipswich fans adopted it and put it on scarves.
questions.why: The best nicknames began as insults. This is the textbook example.
questions.use: "Tractor Boys started as an insult. Ipswich just took it and ran."

questions.question: Ipswich beat Norwich 3-1 in October 2025. It was their first derby win in how many years?
questions.explanation: Sixteen. They won at Carrow Road in April 2026 too, their first league double over Norwich since 1992-93.
questions.why: Rivalries tell you who he shouts at. That season he shouted happily.
questions.use: Ask him: "Sixteen years without beating Norwich. How good was that season?"

questions.question: In which year was Ipswich Town founded?
questions.explanation: 1878, though they stayed amateur until 1936 and joined the Football League in 1938. Late starters who then went all the way to the top.
questions.why: From amateur club to champions in a generation is a remarkable arc.
questions.use: "Ipswich were amateurs until 1936. Within a generation they were champions of England."

questions.question: In which year did Ipswich win the league title?
questions.explanation: 1962, in their very first season in the top division, a year after winning the second tier.
questions.why: Winning the league in your first top-flight season is a fact rival fans struggle to top.
questions.use: "Ipswich won the title in their first ever season in the top division. 1962."

questions.question: Which future England manager took Ipswich from the third tier to league champions?
questions.explanation: Alf Ramsey, who arrived in 1955 with the club in the third tier and went on to win the World Championship with England. His statue stands outside the ground.
questions.why: Ipswich gave England the manager who won the 1966 World Championship. A national-level fact.
questions.use: "Alf Ramsey made England world champions in 1966. He learned how at Ipswich."

questions.question: In which year did Ipswich win the FA Cup?
questions.explanation: 1978, beating Arsenal 1-0 at Wembley. The scorer was so overcome he had to be substituted straight afterwards.
questions.why: A goalscorer subbed off for fainting with emotion is a story worth the telling.
questions.use: "The guy who scored Ipswich's cup final winner had to come off straight after. Overcome."

questions.question: Which European trophy did Ipswich win in 1981?
questions.explanation: The UEFA Cup, over a two-legged final, 5-4 on aggregate, with a side that played lovely football.
questions.why: A town club winning a European trophy is the kind of thing that sounds made up.
questions.use: "Ipswich won a European trophy in 1981. And it's a town, not even a city."

questions.question: Which manager led Ipswich from 1969 to 1982, then took the England job?
questions.explanation: Bobby Robson, who went on to manage England, Barcelona and Newcastle. His statue stands outside the ground.
questions.why: Robson is one of English football's best-loved figures. Knowing where he started is a kindness.
questions.use: "Bobby Robson learned his trade at Ipswich. Thirteen years before England."

questions.question: Which Northern Irish manager took Ipswich from League One to the Premier League in 2023 and 2024?
questions.explanation: Kieran McKenna, back-to-back promotions in his first two full seasons, after 22 years out of the top flight. Big clubs came calling and he stayed.
questions.why: Two promotions in a row is rare. McKenna is the name Ipswich fans thank for it.
questions.use: "McKenna took them from the third tier to the Premier League in two seasons."

questions.question: Who did Ipswich beat in their 1981 European final?
questions.explanation: AZ Alkmaar, 3-0 at home and 2-4 away. John Wark, a midfielder, scored 14 goals in the competition that season.
questions.why: The Alkmaar detail separates fans who know from fans who think they know.
questions.use: "They beat AZ Alkmaar in the 1981 final. Their midfielder scored fourteen European goals that year."

questions.question: What colours are Ipswich Town's home shirts?
questions.explanation: Blue shirts and white shorts. Norwich are yellow and green, which makes the derby easy to follow.
questions.why: Kit colours are the first thing you need on match day.
questions.use: "Blue and white is Ipswich. Yellow and green is Norwich. Two different worlds."

questions.question: Who scored the winner when Ipswich beat Arsenal in an FA Cup final?
questions.explanation: Roger Osborne, a local lad, in the 77th minute. He collapsed with emotion and exhaustion and was substituted moments later.
questions.why: Cup final goalscorers become immortal at small clubs. Osborne is Ipswich's.
questions.use: "Roger Osborne. Scored the cup final winner and had to be taken off in tears."

questions.question: Ipswich is in which county?
questions.explanation: Suffolk, on the east coast. Norwich, in Norfolk, is forty miles north and the source of all the trouble.
questions.why: Suffolk versus Norfolk is the whole East Anglian rivalry in two words.
questions.use: "Suffolk. Norwich are Norfolk. That's the whole derby."

questions.question: What animal is on the Ipswich Town badge?
questions.explanation: A carthorse, the county's own heavy farm breed. Norwich have a canary; Ipswich chose a horse.
questions.why: Badge stories are a low-cost way to show attention.
questions.use: "It's a farm horse on the badge. They lean into it."

questions.question: Ipswich were founder members of the Premier League in which season?
questions.explanation: 1992-93, having won the second tier the previous year. They were relegated in 1995 after a 9-0 defeat at Manchester United.
questions.why: Being there at the start of the Premier League is a small badge of honour.
questions.use: "Ipswich were in the very first Premier League season. Then lost 9-0 at Old Trafford and went down."

questions.question: Where did Ipswich finish in 2000-01, their first Premier League season back up?
questions.explanation: Fifth, under George Burley, which took them into Europe. Burley was voted manager of the year.
questions.why: Fifth in the Premier League is the season fans bring up when hopes are high.
questions.use: "They finished fifth in 2001. Above Chelsea. Different times."

questions.question: What tongue-in-cheek name is given to the Ipswich v Norwich derby?
questions.explanation: The Old Farm derby, a joke on the Old Firm, Glasgow's Celtic against Rangers. Both sets of fans use it.
questions.why: A pun both sets of fans use is rare. This is one.
questions.use: "Old Farm derby. Even the fans call it that."

questions.question: Ipswich went straight back down in 2025. Which two clubs went down with them?
questions.explanation: Leicester and Southampton, the other two promoted clubs. It was the second season running that all three promoted sides went straight back down.
questions.why: The yo-yo is the story of the club's mid-2020s. He will have views on which drop hurt more.
questions.use: Ask him: "Was going down in 2025 worse because of how good 2024 had felt?"

questions.question: How did Ipswich win promotion back to the Premier League in 2026?
questions.explanation: Second in the Championship, behind Coventry, which means automatic promotion with no play-offs. One season down, straight back up.
questions.why: The bounce back is the fresh good news. Lead with it.
questions.use: "Second in the Championship. Straight back up, no play-offs needed."

questions.question: What is Leeds United's home ground called?
questions.explanation: Elland Road, famous for being loud and hostile to visitors. Leeds fans consider that a compliment.
questions.why: 'Elland Road under the lights' is a phrase he will say with feeling.
questions.use: "Elland Road on a night game. Properly hostile."

questions.question: What colour do Leeds United play in?
questions.explanation: All white, shirts, shorts and socks, since 1961. Before that Leeds wore blue and gold.
questions.why: All white is the quickest way to spot Leeds on a small screen.
questions.use: "All white. Shirts, shorts, socks. That's Leeds."

questions.question: In which year was Leeds United founded?
questions.explanation: 1919, after the previous club, Leeds City, was expelled from the league for illegal payments to players. A fresh start with a new name.
questions.why: A club born from a scandal is a good origin story.
questions.use: "Leeds United only exist because the old club got kicked out of the league for paying players illegally."

questions.question: Which manager built the great Leeds team of the 1960s and 70s?
questions.explanation: Don Revie, manager 1961 to 1974: two league titles, an FA Cup and a reputation for being brilliant, ruthless and hard to like. Left to manage England.
questions.why: Revie is the founding father of modern Leeds. His statue stands outside the ground.
questions.use: Ask him: "Was Revie's Leeds dirty, or just better than everyone and hated for it?"

questions.question: In which year did Leeds win the league title, the third in the club's history?
questions.explanation: 1992, the final season before the Premier League began. Three titles in total: 1969, 1974 and 1992.
questions.why: Leeds fans point out they were champions the year before the Premier League began. A favourite line.
questions.use: "Leeds were the champions the year before the Premier League started. They like reminding people."

questions.question: Who managed Leeds to their third league title?
questions.explanation: Howard Wilkinson, known as Sergeant Wilko. By 2026 no English manager had won the top division since.
questions.why: That fact comes up whenever an English manager gets a big job.
questions.use: Ask him: "Is it true no English manager has won the league since Howard Wilkinson?"

questions.question: In which year did Leeds reach the semi-finals of the Champions League?
questions.explanation: 2001, losing to Valencia, with a young team that had beaten Deportivo and drawn with Barcelona. Then the money ran out.
questions.why: The 2001 run is the peak before the fall. Fans tell both halves together.
questions.use: Ask him: "Do you remember the 2001 Champions League team? Before it all went wrong?"

questions.question: By which year had Leeds fallen to League One, the third tier, after their financial collapse?
questions.explanation: 2007, three years after leaving the Premier League. They had spent money they expected from the Champions League and it stopped coming. The phrase is 'doing a Leeds'.
questions.why: 'Doing a Leeds' is a warning used about every over-spending club. He will know the phrase.
questions.use: "'Doing a Leeds' means spending money you haven't got. They went from a Champions League semi to the third tier in a few years."

questions.question: Which Argentine manager took Leeds back to the Premier League in 2020?
questions.explanation: Marcelo Bielsa, who sat on a blue bucket, ran the players into the ground and was adored. He ended sixteen years out of the top flight.
questions.why: Bielsa is a cult figure across football. Leeds fans think he is theirs.
questions.use: Ask him: "Bielsa: greatest thing that ever happened to Leeds, or did he burn them out?"

questions.question: Who are Leeds United's fiercest rivals?
questions.explanation: Manchester United, in the Roses rivalry, named after the Wars of the Roses, fought five hundred years before football.
questions.why: A derby with a medieval origin is the one to know.
questions.use: "Leeds and Man United is the Roses rivalry. It goes back to an actual war in the 1400s."

questions.question: Which captain of the 1969 and 1974 title teams has a statue outside the ground?
questions.explanation: Billy Bremner, the small, red-haired Scottish midfielder who was afraid of nobody. The statue went up in 1999.
questions.why: The statue is the meeting point outside the ground. Knowing who it is helps.
questions.use: "That's Billy Bremner. The old captain. Tiny and terrifying."

questions.question: Which old Leeds nickname came from a pub near the ground?
questions.explanation: The Peacocks, after the Old Peacock pub across the road from the ground. The Blades and the Owls are the two Sheffield clubs.
questions.why: An obscure nickname impresses more than the obvious one.
questions.use: "Leeds used to be called the Peacocks, after a pub by the ground. Hardly anyone says it now."

questions.question: Why did Leeds switch to their famous kit in 1961?
options: To match the city's coat of arms
questions.explanation: The new manager changed it to copy Real Madrid, winners of the first five European Cups, hoping his players would carry themselves like champions.
questions.why: The kit as a psychological trick is a great story about ambition.
questions.use: "They changed the kit to copy Real Madrid. Then they started winning."

questions.question: Leeds lost the 1975 European Cup final to which club?
questions.explanation: Bayern Munich, 2-0 in Paris, after a Leeds goal was ruled out and two penalty shouts refused. Fans rioted and Leeds were banned from Europe.
questions.why: The 1975 final is the great Leeds grievance. Knowing it earns you a long, passionate story.
questions.use: Ask him: "Paris 1975. Were Leeds robbed, honestly?"

questions.question: Leeds returned to the Premier League in 2025 as Championship champions with how many points?
questions.explanation: One hundred, level with Burnley, decided on the final day. Both went up, and Leeds took the title on goal difference.
questions.why: A hundred points is a number he will quote. Have it ready.
questions.use: "A hundred points and it came down to goal difference on the final day."

questions.question: What is the name of the Leeds United club song?
questions.explanation: Marching On Together, released as a single for the 1972 FA Cup final and sung at every game since. The words are on the wall outside the ground.
questions.why: He knows every word. You can know the title.
questions.use: "Marching On Together. That's the one they all sing."

questions.question: Leeds won the FA Cup in 1972 by beating which club?
questions.explanation: Arsenal, 1-0 in the centenary final, with an Allan Clarke diving header. By 2026 it was the club's one FA Cup win.
questions.why: One FA Cup, by 2026, is a stat that surprises people about a club this big.
questions.use: "Leeds won the FA Cup in 1972. The centenary final, with a diving header."

questions.question: Leeds is in which county?
questions.explanation: West Yorkshire. The white rose on the badge is the county's symbol.
questions.why: Yorkshire is not a county to Yorkshire people; it is a nationality. Get it right.
questions.use: "Yorkshire. Don't say 'up north' to a Leeds fan, say Yorkshire."

questions.question: Which player did Leeds sell to Manchester United in the 1990s, a deal they came to regret?
questions.explanation: Eric Cantona, in November 1992, for about £1.2 million. He won four titles in five years at Old Trafford.
questions.why: Selling Cantona is the transfer Leeds fans wince at.
questions.use: "Leeds sold Cantona to Man United for about a million. Then he won four titles for them."

questions.question: Which German manager led Leeds to promotion in 2025?
questions.explanation: Daniel Farke, who had already taken Norwich up twice, in 2019 and 2021. He knew the Championship inside out.
questions.why: Farke is the name on the 2025 promotion. Fans judge him on what came after.
questions.use: Ask him: "Was Farke the man for the Premier League, or just brilliant in the Championship?"

questions.question: What is Liverpool's home ground called?
questions.explanation: Anfield, since 1892. It was Everton's ground first, until a rent row saw Everton leave and the landlord start a new club to play there.
questions.why: Liverpool exist because of a landlord dispute. Evertonians love telling this; get in first.
questions.use: "Liverpool were founded because Everton fell out with their landlord over rent at Anfield."

questions.question: Which song do Liverpool fans sing before every home match?
questions.explanation: You'll Never Walk Alone, a show tune from the musical Carousel, adopted in 1963 after a Liverpool band had a hit with it. The words are on the gates at the ground.
questions.why: A football anthem that began life as a Broadway ballad.
questions.use: "You'll Never Walk Alone is from a musical. Carousel, 1945. They took it from a pop cover."

questions.question: Liverpool's league title in 2025 was the club's how-manyth?
questions.explanation: Twentieth, drawing level with Manchester United. The nineteenth had ended a thirty-year wait.
questions.why: Twenty versus United's twenty is the count he keeps. Know the number.
questions.use: "Twenty titles by 2025. Level with United. That's the argument at every family dinner."

questions.question: How many times had Liverpool won the European Cup or Champions League by 2025?
questions.explanation: Six: 1977, 1978, 1981, 1984, 2005 and 2019. By 2025 no other English club had as many, which Liverpool fans mention regularly.
questions.why: Six European Cups is the number that ends arguments with United fans.
questions.use: "Six European Cups. Ask a United fan how many they've got."

questions.question: Liverpool came back from 3-0 down to win the 2005 Champions League final against which club?
questions.explanation: AC Milan, in Istanbul: 3-0 down at half-time, three goals in six minutes early in the second half, then won on penalties. The miracle of Istanbul.
questions.why: Istanbul is the comeback every football fan knows. Every Liverpool fan can tell you where they were.
questions.use: Ask him: "Istanbul 2005. Where were you at half-time?"

questions.question: Which German managed Liverpool from 2015 to 2024?
questions.explanation: Jürgen Klopp: hugs, heavy-metal football, a Champions League and a league title after thirty years. He left as one of the best-loved managers the club had known.
questions.why: Klopp is the manager she has probably heard of even without football. He is the reference point.
questions.use: "Klopp. Nine years, everyone loved him, then he just left on his own terms."

questions.question: In which year did Liverpool end their thirty-year wait for a league title?
questions.explanation: 2020, during the pandemic, with seven games to spare and an empty stadium. Fans celebrated outside the ground anyway.
questions.why: Thirty years of waiting then no crowd to celebrate is the bittersweet note in the story.
questions.use: Ask him: "Winning it in lockdown with no fans in. Did it feel real?"

questions.question: Which striker scored 346 goals for Liverpool across two spells in the 1980s and 90s?
questions.explanation: Ian Rush, a Welsh striker with a moustache and a knack for scoring against Everton. By 2025 nobody had scored more for the club.
questions.why: Rush is the name older fans reach for whenever goalscorers come up.
questions.use: Ask him: "Will anyone ever catch Ian Rush's 346?"

questions.question: Which two clubs are Liverpool's main rivals?
questions.explanation: Everton, across the park, in the Merseyside derby; and Manchester United, thirty miles away, a rivalry built on decades of fighting over trophies.
questions.why: Two rivals, two different kinds of hate. Knowing which is which matters.
questions.use: "Everton's the local one. United's the real one."

questions.question: The Kop, Anfield's famous stand, is named after what?
options: A hill in the Boer War
questions.explanation: Spion Kop, a hill in South Africa where many soldiers from Liverpool died in a battle in 1900. The steep terrace reminded people of it.
questions.why: The name has a war behind it. That is worth knowing before you shout it.
questions.use: "The Kop's named after a hill in the Boer War where Liverpool soldiers died."

questions.question: Which Scot managed Liverpool from 1959 to 1974 and has a statue outside Anfield?
questions.explanation: Bill Shankly, who took them up from the second division and built the modern club. The Shankly Gates went up in his honour in 1982, and his quotes turn up everywhere.
questions.why: Shankly quotes get used at every Liverpool occasion. Know the man behind them.
questions.use: "Shankly said football's more important than life and death. He was joking. Mostly."

questions.question: Which Liverpool manager won three European Cups between 1977 and 1981?
questions.explanation: Bob Paisley, the quiet assistant who stepped up in 1974 and turned out to be even more successful: six league titles and three European Cups in nine years.
questions.why: The quiet assistant who out-won his famous boss is a lovely twist to know.
questions.use: "Paisley won three European Cups. Nobody talks about him because he didn't do quotes."

questions.question: Steven Gerrard's long-range equaliser in the 2006 FA Cup final came against which club?
questions.explanation: West Ham, in the final minute, from 35 yards, with cramp. Liverpool won on penalties. People call it the Gerrard final.
questions.why: A final named after one player tells you what he meant to them.
questions.use: "The Gerrard final. Thirty-five yards, last minute, cramp in both legs."

questions.question: Mohamed Salah joined Liverpool in 2017 from which club?
questions.explanation: Roma, for about £37 million, after Chelsea had given up on him. He scored 44 goals in his first season.
questions.why: Chelsea letting Salah go is the transfer regret rivals enjoy raising.
questions.use: Ask him: "Is Salah the best signing Liverpool have ever made?"

questions.question: Virgil van Dijk joined Liverpool in 2018 from which club?
questions.explanation: Southampton, for £75 million, a world record for a defender at the time. Liverpool reached the next two Champions League finals with him.
questions.why: Van Dijk changed Liverpool overnight. The fee looked mad and then looked cheap.
questions.use: "Seventy-five million for a defender looked mad. Then they won everything."

questions.question: Who took over at Liverpool in 2024 and won the title in his first season?
questions.explanation: Arne Slot, from Feyenoord. Calm where his predecessor was loud, and champion within a year.
questions.why: Following a legend and winning the league immediately is rare. Slot did it.
questions.use: Ask him: "Did Slot win that title, or was it the team he inherited?"

questions.question: Who did Liverpool beat in the 2019 Champions League final?
questions.explanation: Tottenham, 2-0 in Madrid, with a penalty in the second minute, a year after losing the final to Real Madrid.
questions.why: An all-English final is the kind of night that gets relived. He will remember the penalty.
questions.use: "Madrid 2019. Penalty in the second minute and that was that."

questions.question: In the 2019 comeback against Barcelona, who took the quick corner for the winning goal?
questions.explanation: Trent Alexander-Arnold, a local lad, while Barcelona's defenders were not looking. Divock Origi tapped it in to complete a 4-0 win from 3-0 down.
questions.why: 'Corner taken quickly' is a phrase Liverpool fans say as a catchphrase. This is why.
questions.use: "'Corner taken quickly, Origi.' That's the commentary from the Barcelona game. Fans quote it."

questions.question: What bird is on the Liverpool badge?
questions.explanation: The liver bird, the city's symbol, a cormorant with a sprig of seaweed in its beak. It is on the town hall and the Liver Building too.
questions.why: Reading the badge is knowing the city.
questions.use: "That's the liver bird. It's all over the city, not just the club."

questions.question: Kenny Dalglish joined Liverpool in 1977 from which club?
questions.explanation: Celtic, for £440,000, to replace Kevin Keegan. He became a club great, then its manager, and won the league in both roles.
questions.why: King Kenny is the name older fans say with reverence. A stand at the ground carries his name.
questions.use: "King Kenny. Player, manager, won the league as both. There's a stand named after him."

questions.question: What is Manchester City's home ground called?
questions.explanation: The Etihad Stadium, built for the 2002 Commonwealth Games and converted for football. Officially the City of Manchester Stadium.
questions.why: An athletics stadium turned football ground is a good bit of context.
questions.use: "The Etihad was built for the Commonwealth Games. City moved in after."

questions.question: Where did Manchester City play before they moved grounds in 2003?
questions.explanation: Maine Road, in Moss Side, from 1923 to 2003. In 1934 it held 84,569 for an FA Cup game against Stoke.
questions.why: Older City fans get misty about Maine Road. It is where the club's soul lived before the money.
questions.use: Ask him: "Did you ever go to Maine Road? Everyone says it was a different club then."

questions.question: What colour are Manchester City's home shirts?
questions.explanation: Sky blue, since the 1890s. The fans' song is Blue Moon, sung slowly and sadly, which suited the club for much of its history.
questions.why: Blue Moon before every game is one of football's odder rituals. Knowing why it is sad helps.
questions.use: "Blue Moon. They sing it slow, from when City were rubbish. It stuck."

questions.question: Which Spanish manager took charge of Manchester City in 2016?
questions.explanation: Pep Guardiola, who had won everything at Barcelona and Bayern. Six league titles in his first eight seasons at City and a treble in 2023.
questions.why: Guardiola is the manager every other manager is compared to. His City years are the benchmark.
questions.use: Ask him: "Is Guardiola the best manager there's ever been, or did the money do it?"

questions.question: In which year was Manchester City bought by Abu Dhabi's Sheikh Mansour?
questions.explanation: 2008, on the final day of the transfer window. They signed Robinho the same afternoon and the modern City began.
questions.why: Everything about City splits into before and after 2008.
questions.use: "2008. Before that they were a joke club. After that, well."

questions.question: In which year did Manchester City win their first Premier League title?
questions.explanation: 2012, with Agüero's goal in the final seconds of the final game against QPR, to beat United on goal difference. Their first title since 1968.
questions.why: The Agüero moment is the one every football fan remembers, City or not.
questions.use: "Agüerooo. Last kick of the season. Even neutrals remember where they were."

questions.question: Which English club won the league, FA Cup and European Cup treble before City did in 2023?
questions.explanation: Manchester United, in 1999, under Alex Ferguson. City matching United's treble was a big part of the joy.
questions.why: The treble is the peak of the Guardiola era, and the United comparison is half the fun.
questions.use: "2023 treble. United had done it in 1999, and City loved matching it."

questions.question: Who did Manchester City beat in the 2023 Champions League final?
questions.explanation: Inter Milan, 1-0 in Istanbul, with a goal from Rodri. Their first European Cup, after years of trying.
questions.why: The first European Cup is the trophy City fans waited longest for.
questions.use: "Rodri scored the goal in Istanbul. First European Cup, finally."

questions.question: How many goals did Erling Haaland score in the 2022-23 Premier League season?
questions.explanation: Thirty-six, in his first season in England, beating a mark that had stood since 1994. Also 52 in all competitions.
questions.why: Thirty-six is the number he will quote when defending Haaland in any argument.
questions.use: "Thirty-six league goals in his first season. In England. At 22."

questions.question: In 2024 City became the first English club to win how many consecutive league titles?
questions.explanation: Four in a row, 2021 to 2024. Nobody had done more than three before.
questions.why: Four in a row is the argument for that City side being the best England had produced.
questions.use: "Four titles in a row. Nobody had ever done that in England."

questions.question: What did Alex Ferguson call City in 2009, after the money arrived?
options: The small club down the road
questions.explanation: The noisy neighbours, a jibe from United's manager once City started spending big. City fans took it as a compliment.
questions.why: The derby decides who owns Manchester that week, and this line is part of the story.
questions.use: "The noisy neighbours. Ferguson's line. Aged badly for him."

questions.question: In the 1999 play-off final against Gillingham, who scored City's 95th-minute equaliser?
questions.explanation: Paul Dickov, at Wembley, with City 2-0 down and in the third tier. They won on penalties. Fans talk about it as the goal that saved the club.
questions.why: City in the third division in 1999 is the fact that makes the modern club astonishing.
questions.use: "City were in the third division in 1999. Hard to believe now, isn't it?"

questions.question: In which year did Manchester City win the European Cup Winners' Cup?
questions.explanation: 1970, beating Górnik Zabrze of Poland in Vienna. Their one European trophy until 2023.
questions.why: City fans of a certain age had one European trophy to cling to for fifty years. This is it.
questions.use: "City won a European trophy in 1970 and then nothing in Europe until 2023."
